transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 08:47 PT
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Partner Ops), Daniel Hsu (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (BrightBridge GM), Sana Patel (BrightBridge Head of Solutions), Ethan Wu (BrightBridge Sales Director), Marisol Gomez (BrightBridge Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be partial):
Quick partner co-sell warroom to triage top-of-pipeline deals, assign action owners for pilots, align on joint messaging and legal/ procurement gating items. Discussed three priority opportunities (retail AI assistant, financial document extraction, contact center summarization) and risk mitigation (SLA/ data residency/ SOC2). Agreed next steps for joint deck, pilot dates, and technical benchmarks.

Topics detected: co-sell prioritization; pilot scoping; legal gating; benchmarks/latency; joint GTM assets.

Transcript:
00:00 - Avery: All righty, good morning everyone, thanks for joining the channel warroom. I see folks on both sides — Liam, Sana, yeah thanks for making time. We're about an hour, we'll triage the list and leave with clear owners. 
00:14 - Liam: Morning, thanks. Quick ask — we want clarity on which deals BrightBridge should prioritize for the joint pilot, basically where Redwood's runtime gives us a clear win versus the cloud-native offering.
00:28 - Miguel: Totally, and just to frame it, we'll call out latency-sensitive and PII-sensitive deals as high priority because Redwood's Dedicated/Private options are where we can differentiate. Apologies, sometimes I say Dedicate, typo there, I mean Dedicated.
00:42 - Sana: Good. Also our buyers keep asking about audit stuff — SOC2, SSO, and whether we can do a VPC peering setup. 
00:52 - Daniel: We can support VPC connectivity in Private and we have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys, there's an ops checklist we can share. I'll flag that as an item. 
01:05 - Ethan: On the sales side, price sensitivity is real — they're comparing against Bedrock and the internal infra teams. We need crisp TCO examples. 
01:16 - Priya: We'll add templated TCO slides to the co-sell pack. Avery, can you walk through the top three deals you and Liam picked?
01:27 - Avery: Sure — we have Deal A (Retail AI assistant) — target for 2026 Q1 pilot, wants sub-200ms p95 token latency on 512 tokens, has customer data residency in EU; Deal B (FS Document Extraction) — PII handling and retention limits; Deal C (Contact Center Summarization) — high concurrency, cost sensitive.
01:45 - Liam: Yes, those maps. For Deal A the buyer is skeptical of Bedrock's latency at scale, they asked for benchmark runs. For Deal B legal flagged that logs cannot leave country.
01:58 - Miguel: For the retail use case, continuous batching helps cost but might add tail latency; we should propose a hybrid routing: hot-path to Dedicated in region, fallback to Hosted for overflow. Note, our routing can do region + variant fallback but we'll doc constraints.
02:13 - Sana: Can you explain the fallback more? Because the buyer was worried about degraded quality if it falls back.
02:20 - Daniel: Right, so fallback would be to a compatible model family — same arch but lower FP or quantized variant; quality regression is possible, we'll show expected delta from our evals. We should include an observable flag in the route to alert on quality drift.
02:36 - Avery: Action item — Miguel will draft fallback policy language and expected perf delta for Deal A.
02:42 - Miguel: Yep, I'll take that.
02:45 - 03:10 - [general cross-talk, brief audio glitch]
03:11 - Marisol: From legal, vendor questionnaire — can Redwood confirm encryption at rest, KMS support, and audit log retention defaults? Also we need any SOC2 Attestations.
03:22 - Avery: We have SOC2 Type II report — we'll share the kit, and encryption/KMS details. I think the standard retention is 30 days for logs but enterprise options exist.
03:33 - Marisol: Can you send the link to the attestation? Preferably by Friday.
03:37 - Avery: Yes, I'll send by Friday EOD.
03:40 - 05:05 - [deal-by-deal triage segment]
05:06 - Avery: Deal A notes — priority 1 for joint pilot. Open risks: EU data residency, p95 latency target, and model hot swap risk. Proposed mitigations: region-dedicated pool, on-prem gateway option for EU, and run a small-scale benchmark with their sample prompt set.
05:25 - Liam: The on-prem gateway could be heavy — they asked if VPC + logging redaction is acceptable first.
05:34 - Daniel: Yes VPC + log redaction is less invasive; if that's acceptable it's faster. We'll propose both options in the packet.
05:45 - Avery: Deal B — regulatory heavy. We should identify whether they need air-gapped on-prem or if Private with strict KMS and audit is enough.
05:55 - Sana: The customer compliance team tends to prefer on-prem when retention can't be guaranteed. But some will accept Private with contractual SLAs.
06:05 - Miguel: Technical ask for DB-extraction flow — what's the sequence length distribution? If it's long sequences we may need to recommend chunking + embeddings for rerank, that impacts latency but lowers cost.
06:20 - Ethan: Sales note — if we recommend a chunk/embeddings approach, buyers might fling back at model quality, so we need clear artifacts.
06:28 - Avery: We'll include a small demo notebook showing chunking + retrieval followed by generation and expected latencies. Miguel, Daniel on notebook?
06:36 - Daniel: I'll own the notebook; Miguel will add perf numbers.
06:39 - Miguel: Yep.
07:00 - 15:00 - [deep triage, timestamps every 60-90s, omitted for brevity with highlights]
15:12 - Miguel: Quick interjection — for the contact center use case high concurrency means batching then streaming must be tuned. We can recommend a lower max concurrency per GPU and a scaled pool. Also mention KV cash — my typo, I mean KV cache — to avoid repeated context costs.
15:29 - Sana: Good catch. We need guidance to the BrightBridge sellers on how to position these tuning knobs vs naive cloud endpoints.
15:38 - Priya: We'll make a cheat-sheet for sellers: 1) when to pitch Dedicated, 2) when to pitch Dedicated+Private, 3) sample ROI calc.
15:46 - Liam: On the GTM side, what's the co-sell motion? Do we expect Redwood AE to join early meetings or only after qualification?
15:55 - Avery: We proposed an early SE-assisted discovery for pilot targets. Redwood AE will join commercial stages. For enterprise we can do joint exec briefings.
16:06 - Ethan: What about logo use and joint press? Need to confirm BrightBridge permissions for co-marketing.
16:12 - Liam: We'll confirm list of allowed logos and any embargo windows.
16:18 - Daniel: Also technical deep dive — we should set a date. Who's the PD (product) owner on the BrightBridge side?
16:25 - Sana: That would be me. Week of Oct 20 works.
16:31 - Miguel: Noted, I'll schedule an SE deep-dive session.
16:35 - 24:00 - [legal and procurement micro-discussion]
24:03 - Marisol: A couple procurement points — preferred contract term length, data residency verbs, and indemnity for model outputs. We need Redwood's stance on output liability.
24:17 - Avery: Standard approach: we have recital language; for legal we'd need to review specific indemnity asks. For model outputs, we usually carve out content-related risk but we can discuss obligation boundaries. 
24:33 - Marisol: We'll send redlines to the vendor questionnaire and initial SOW.
24:38 - Avery: Great, we'll review and aim to respond within 3 business days.
24:44 - Marisol: Also any partner rebate structure or co-sell discount need to be captured for pricing. 
24:51 - Priya: We have a partner discount tier sheet — I'll attach the appropriate line items to the co-sell deck.
25:01 - 33:00 - [back-and-forth on pricing bands and anchor examples; some speakers overlap]
33:07 - Liam: On pilots, can we do a pilot credit structure with a kickoff MOU? Buyers like a small credit to prove value.
33:16 - Avery: We can do pilot credits for qualified pilots, usually time-boxed 4-8 weeks. We'll draft a sample MOU.
33:25 - Miguel: Technical pilot plan: 1) baseline metric collection; 2) Redwood runs benchmark (latency, p95/p99, cost); 3) joint eval; 4) production plan. I'll put a template in the pipeline sheet.
33:39 - Sana: For Deal B's PII concerns can we redact in-transit logs?
33:45 - Daniel: We can redact logs at ingress when configured; need to verify for the specific fields but that's supported.
33:52 - Marisol: Please include confirmation of retention windows in writing — legal will not accept verbal.
33:59 - Avery: Noted.
34:10 - 44:00 - [planning the joint co-sell deck and pipeline sheet; participants sharing screen briefly, audio artifacts]
44:12 - Priya: I'll own the co-sell deck. Outline: joint value props, deal prioritization matrix, pilot templates, TCO examples, partner program incentives.
44:22 - Liam: Add a slide with competitive differentiators — low latency, private deployments, predictable unit economics.
44:30 - Ethan: Also include how we handle model upgrades and rollbacks — buyers ask that.
44:36 - Miguel: Good point. We'll add an ops slide about rollouts, canarying and fallback. 
44:43 - Avery: Recap of owners: Priya deck, Miguel fallback policy and benchmark plan, Daniel notebook + demo, Marisol will send legal redlines, Liam to confirm pilot accounts.
44:56 - Marisol: I'll get questionnaire over by Friday.
45:02 - Liam: We'll lock in pilot accounts by Monday, tentatively.
45:08 - Avery: Next meeting — SE deep dive week of Oct 20, co-sell sync 2025-10-14 to review deck and pipeline. Does that work for everyone?
45:18 - Sana: Works.
45:21 - Miguel: Works.
45:23 - Priya: Works.
45:25 - Ethan: Works.
45:29 - 54:30 - [closing remarks, small talk, some overlapping goodbye]
54:31 - Avery: Thanks all. I'll send the action list and the co-sell sheet after the call.
54:37 - Liam: Appreciate it. Talk soon.

End of transcript.
